page.title: Microservices Architecture
page.scope: 6 standalone services · broker-mediated · monolith or split deployment
page.summary: Rocket.Chat's backend uses a service-oriented monolith architecture where business logic is divided into 6 services that can either run in a single process via an in-memory broker or be deployed as separate microservices for scaling. Services communicate through a broker abstraction rather than importing each other directly, making the deployment model flexible: you can run everything in one container or split services into standalone deployments.

prose.text: Rocket.Chat's backend is a **service-oriented monolith**: business logic is grouped into services that can run **in-process** (single deployment, via the in-memory broker) or be **split out** into standalone microservices for horizontal scaling. 6 services are packaged for standalone deployment under `ee/apps/`.

| Service | Purpose | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `@rocket.chat/account-service` | Rocket.Chat Account service | ee/apps/account-service/package.json:1 |
| `@rocket.chat/authorization-service` | Rocket.Chat Authorization service | ee/apps/authorization-service/package.json:1 |
| `@rocket.chat/ddp-streamer` | Rocket.Chat DDP-Streamer service | ee/apps/ddp-streamer/package.json:1 |
| `@rocket.chat/omnichannel-transcript` | Rocket.Chat service | ee/apps/omnichannel-transcript/package.json:1 |
| `@rocket.chat/presence-service` | Rocket.Chat Presence service | ee/apps/presence-service/package.json:1 |
| `@rocket.chat/queue-worker` | Rocket.Chat service | ee/apps/queue-worker/package.json:1 |
prose.narrative: Six services are packaged for independent deployment under `ee/apps/`: account-service handles authentication, authorization-service manages permissions, ddp-streamer handles real-time subscriptions, omnichannel-transcript manages conversation archives, presence-service tracks user status, and queue-worker processes asynchronous jobs.

prose.text:
Services never import each other directly — they talk through the broker abstraction:

- **`@rocket.chat/core-services`** — service interfaces + registry. Services register here and call each other through it, transport-agnostic.
  - In-process (monolith) transport: `packages/core-services/src/LocalBroker.ts` — routes calls in memory, no network.

Sources: packages/core-services/src/index.ts:1, packages/core-services/src/LocalBroker.ts:1
prose.narrative: Services never directly import each other—instead they register with and call through `@rocket.chat/core-services`, which provides transport-agnostic service interfaces. In monolith mode, `LocalBroker` routes all calls in memory without network overhead; in microservices mode, a network broker connects services across containers.

prose.text:
| Mode | Transport | When |
|---|---|---|
| Monolith | in-memory broker (`LocalBroker`) | single container; services run in one process |
| Microservices | network broker | services in `ee/apps/` run as separate containers, scaled independently |
prose.narrative: The monolith mode uses an in-memory broker to run all services in one process within a single container, ideal for simple deployments. Microservices mode uses a network broker so services in `ee/apps/` run as separate containers that can be scaled independently based on load.
